SwartzNet Hexagonal Rebuild — "The Wire Lives Only in Adapters"

per_proposal.proposal_name: SwartzNet Rebuild — "Keep the Seams, Kill the Defect Classes"

strengths: Most spec-grounded of the three: nearly every key decision carries an explicit §-reference, and it enumerates a concrete structural fix for essentially every §6.1 defect (capability drift, publisher-bit clobber, sequential /search, admission inversion, trusted-publisher demotion, reputation-feedback inconsistency, ZIM shim, first-token lookup, RIBLT one-batch, companion attribution, env dual-gate, wrong license, slot accounting).

The capability.Announced() single-producer decision is a genuine structural fix that kills three distinct §6 wire defects at once (capability-downgrade-not-on-wire, /aggregate static 0x2ED, and the drift between them) by construction — there is exactly one function, so wire mask and readout provably cannot disagree.

Splitting operator-settable Sharing from daemon-owned RuntimeFacts makes the §6 'Save sharing clobbers the Publisher bit' defect literally unrepresentable — the HTTP setter's type cannot reach the Publisher bit.

Extracting a leaf `record` package owning SignedRecord/SigMessage()/ElementID() directly targets the §5.1 byte-identical-derivation-in-two-files hazard without breaking layer isolation (record is format-neutral, not a cross-layer response type).

Promotes the MiniPeer + golden-wire-vector conformance suite (wirecompat) into the CI merge gate, converting invariant #1 from a convention into an enforced gate — the single most load-bearing invariant.
Build order mirrors a known-working structure, so integration risk is low and each slice ships genuinely observable behavior.

Preserves the strict §5.8 httpapi law best of the three: ZERO subsystem imports, narrow interfaces, DTOs re-declared locally — searchmux returns a tuple of the three native response types and the daemon adapter translates field-by-field.
weaknesses: Enforces 'never send sn_search to a non-advertising peer' via a per-connection runtime fact rather than a type-level guarantee (proposals 2 and 3 make it unforgeable at the type level) — golden vectors + wirecompat gate compensate but it is structurally weaker for that one rule.

The engine module remains a fat integration hub depending on ~11 packages, inheriting the legacy's central-hub shape; RuntimeFacts must be recomputed at exactly the right moments or advertising silently drifts.
Layer-D swap is handled by a RecordBackend seam inside dhtindex, but Bleve stays inside indexer with no swap port, so the recorded tantivy/FTS5 migration is less clean than a fully porterized design.
Only explicitly names slot-accounting defect (a) (Bloom-nil skips promotion); the second half of §6.1 (all-files-set-to-none permanently occupying a slot) is not called out.

Deny-by-default admission with an empty shipped anchor list means cold-start is correct but inert without operator keys — flagged as a release prerequisite, not code, but still a live gap (§6.2, §7-B).
best_ideas_to_graft: capability.Announced(Sharing, RuntimeFacts) as the SINGLE producer of the 64-bit services mask, consumed identically by swarmsearch peer_announce and httpapi's ServicesReporter.
Type-split operator Sharing vs daemon RuntimeFacts so partial HTTP POSTs physically cannot zero the Publisher bit.
A leaf `record` package (SignedRecord/SigMessage/ElementID) imported by swarmsearch, dhtindex, and companion so the byte-identical derivation cannot drift.

Promote MiniPeer + frozen golden wire-vectors into the CI merge gate (assert non-advertising peer receives zero sn_search frames, vanilla anacrolix completes a download, BEP-44 items indistinguishable).
A single searchmux shared by daemon-adapter AND gui so concurrent fan-out and reconciliation exist once, and web/GUI cannot diverge.
Centralize confirm/flag in ONE daemon path (consulting trust.IsTrusted before demotion) so all frontends agree and trusted publishers are exempt.
Define the Layer-D RecordBackend seam against the legacy path FIRST and only add the aggregate impl once legacy passes the full lookup suite.
evaluation.overall: The strongest proposal on exactly the axes weighted highest. It reproduces §2 breadth, preserves the subtle §5 rules by keeping every wire byte in leaf codecs plus a shared record package, and converts the §6 defect classes from 'possible' to 'unrepresentable' by relocating each root cause into one small owner. It is also the most feasible and among the simplest, because it evolves rather than reinvents the legacy package map. Its only relative shortfalls — a runtime rather than type-level peer-advertisement guard, and a less-porterized Bleve seam — are outweighed by its exhaustive, citation-anchored §6 coverage and its promotion of wire-compat to a hard gate.

per_proposal.proposal_name: SwartzNet Hexagonal Rebuild — "The Wire Lives Only in Adapters"

strengths: Strongest structural story for the load-bearing invariant #1: every vanilla-observable byte originates in exactly four adapter packages, and LtepTransport.SendExtension REQUIRES a capability-verified peer token minted only from a recorded sn_search advertisement — 'never send to a non-advertising peer' becomes a type-level property, not a runtime check.

Best seam-swappability of the three by a wide margin: KeywordDirectory is one port with legacy/aggregate/composite implementations, so the §5.2 ≥12-month dual-read contract is expressed as a composite adapter with ZERO app/domain change, and selecting the Layer-D format is one line in node.New; RecordCodec is a separate port so record bytes stay codec-owned.

Puts the three cross-implementation contracts (Tokenize, Chunker, RecordID) and two frozen file formats (reputation score, Bloom double-hash) in a stdlib-only core imported by every adapter — making the §5.1/§5.5/§5.6 drift hazards a compile-time impossibility.

Enables the wire-compat matrix to run in-process against an in-memory VanillaPeer double implementing the transport port, decomposing invariant-1 testing into cheap independent tiers while retaining the real anacrolix interop as belt-and-suspenders.

Explicitly enumerates and quarantines the anacrolix §5.4 quirks (positive burst, async off-read-loop dispatch, VerifyData rehash, seed-in-place FilePathMaker, PeerStore write tokens, Exp=2h) inside the two anacrolix adapters, so those rules are named, not lost.
Localhost-only API is structurally guaranteed: no application port carries any auth concept, so a remote authenticated mode cannot appear by accident.
weaknesses: Least simple by a clear margin: 7 core packages + a ports package with 12 driven and 8 driving interfaces + an app layer + ~12 adapters + node. Every cross-boundary call is a port-speaking-core-types indirection — heavy ceremony for a domain saturated with anacrolix-shaped quirks.

The SwarmEngine port is wide (snapshots, per-file priority, LTEP callbacks, storage override, VerifyData) and risks ossifying into an anacrolix-shaped interface — the proposal admits the async-lock and rehash quirks cannot be abstracted away.

Relocates reconciliation into app.SearchService returning a shared core/search.CombinedSearch container consumed by all frontends — this respects 'no merged HIT type' but introduces a shared cross-layer container, a mild deviation from §5.8's 'three response types reconciled only at the httpapi boundary'.

Higher upfront integration risk: S0 requires building the entire core + ports + in-memory adapters + golden vectors before the first real download, and the ports over anacrolix must be drawn correctly early or churn.
KeywordDirectory risks becoming a lowest-common-denominator port between a CAS-RMW per-keyword model and a B-tree/RIBLT model — acknowledged and mitigated, but a real design tension.
best_ideas_to_graft: LtepTransport.SendExtension requiring a capability-verified peer token minted only from a recorded sn_search advertisement — turning the 'only advertised peers' rule into a type-level guarantee.
KeywordDirectory port with legacy + aggregate + a COMPOSITE dual-write/dual-read adapter, plus a separate RecordCodec port, as the cleanest expression of the §0/§5.2 migration seam.
An in-memory VanillaPeer test double implementing the transport port, so the four-direction wire matrix runs as in-process unit tests with the real anacrolix client kept as a non-unit gate.
IdentityVault.Load/Create returning an isDefaultPath flag so 'auto-create only at the XDG default, never regenerate implicitly' is domain policy rather than scattered checks.
Implementing L1 in-swarm sharing as a LocalIndex query filtered to the domain-owned active-swarm set — making the §6 'L1 shares nothing' defect into a real, cheap feature.
evaluation.overall: The most elegant invariant and swappability story of the three — the type-level SendExtension token and the KeywordDirectory/composite seam are the cleanest structural guarantees on offer, and frozen formats live in a stdlib-only core. But it pays heavily in simplicity and carries the highest upfront integration risk: a large hexagon must be built before the first real byte moves, and the SwarmEngine port must survive contact with anacrolix's many un-abstractable quirks. Its wire-compat and migration structure are best-in-class; its ceremony and the risk of anacrolix-shaped ports keep it second on the weighted axes.

strengths: Slices map directly onto the §2 capability structure, and the build order ships a genuinely user-observable increment at every step (identity → download → local search → trust → sign → DHT → swarm → companion → aggregate → frontends).

kernel/substrate as a policy-free sole owner of the anacrolix client + DHT + LTEP map is a clean containment: no slice can set a reserved bit, open a UDP port, or add a DHT verb because the ports expose no such primitive, and LtepTransport.Send needs a peer handle that only exists post-advertisement (type-level, like proposal 2).

A contracts/* tier of frozen dependency-free leaves (sntoken, snrecord, snsign, dhtschema, snagg, riblt, ltepcodec) each with checked-in golden byte vectors is the best articulation of 'a second implementation is buildable from the leaf + its fixtures' — the strongest §5.1/§2.12 anti-drift move.

Decouples download from its legacy search/DHT/trust hooks by making them event-bus subscribers — and correctly pairs the drop-on-full FileCompleted event with searchlocal's hourly rescan-of-completed-files fallback, preserving the §5.5 backpressure contract.

Fixes the §6 defects it targets cleanly: one live-caps function feeding wire + /aggregate + /capabilities with PATCH (merge) semantics, MostDistinctive-token lookup, deny-by-default admission, verified/attributed companion ingest with GeneratedAt dedup, and a unified env gate.
kernel/lifecycle as the single composition root keeps startup order, degraded-start, and reverse teardown in exactly one place (invariant #4).
weaknesses: frontend/httpapi depends directly on six slices (per-slice route groups) — the loosest of the three against §5.8's 'httpapi must never import engine/companion; three response types reconciled only at the boundary' architectural law; distributing DTO/handler ownership into slices dilutes the isolation guarantee the spec calls law.

The event bus is a second coordination mechanism alongside ports, with drop-on-full and replay-buffer semantics that introduce subtle new failure modes for near-once signalling (e.g. a dropped SignatureTrusted event failing to bloom-confirm a trusted torrent) — more moving parts than a single wiring point, and in tension with the deterministic-state-ownership posture.

kernel/substrate is a single chokepoint all wire flows through; keeping capability logic out of it is guarded by a 'lint/review rule' (discipline) rather than by structure — a regression toward the legacy hub-engine is possible.
'Each slice owns its frontend end-to-end' is only partly enforceable given the CGO/Fyne boundary, so GUI-tab parity for a slice is a convention the compiler will not check.

Layer-D swappability is real (RecordFormat seam in the aggregate slice) but less developed than proposal 2's composite dual-write/dual-read adapter; the ≥12-month legacy-read contract is not expressed as concretely.
best_ideas_to_graft: A contracts/* frozen-leaf tier (tokenizer, record, signing payload, DHT schema, SNAGG, RIBLT, LTEP codec) with checked-in golden byte vectors authored BEFORE the consuming slices, so a wire-compatible second implementation is buildable from the leaf + fixtures alone.

kernel/substrate: a single policy-free owner of the anacrolix client + DHT + rate limiters + LTEP map that exposes only narrow ports and holds zero capability logic, with a review rule that it imports no slice.

Event-bus decoupling of download from search/DHT/trust — letting the download subsystem stay dependency-free — explicitly paired with an hourly rescan fallback so a dropped terminal event is recovered (honors §5.5).
Organizing the build order as vertical capability slices that each ship an observable user increment, mapping 1:1 onto §2.
/capabilities with merge (PATCH) semantics so an omitted field cannot clobber the Publisher bit.
evaluation.overall: A well-balanced, capability-first design whose contracts/* golden-vector tier and policy-free substrate are excellent ideas worth grafting. It fixes the §6 defects it names and preserves the tricky §5.5 event-drop rule. It ranks third because its two structural choices most in tension with the spec's isolation law — httpapi importing six slices, and an event bus as the primary cross-slice channel with drop semantics — add moving parts and slightly loosen the §5.8 'httpapi imports zero subsystems / reconcile only at the boundary' guarantee, while its Layer-D migration seam is less concretely specified than the top two. Strong, but edged out on the weighted spec-completeness and invariant-safety axes.

ranking: SwartzNet Rebuild — "Keep the Seams, Kill the Defect Classes"
SwartzNet Hexagonal Rebuild — "The Wire Lives Only in Adapters"

per_proposal.proposal_name: SwartzNet Rebuild — "Keep the Seams, Kill the Defect Classes"

strengths: Evolves the legacy package map rather than reinventing it, so the smallest possible novel surface area: the only new packages (capability, record, searchmux, admission, wirecompat) each exist to convert one named §6 defect class from 'possible' to 'unrepresentable'. Every module maps 1:1 to a subsystem the SPEC already describes, which is the lowest cognitive and integration cost of the three.

Build order is genuinely a sequence of shippable vertical slices with low integration risk: slice 1 already runs `add` as a downloading+seeding daemon with session restore; each subsequent slice adds one observable capability (local search, web UI, sn_search, concurrent searchmux, Layer D, signing/trust, companion, GUI, Aggregate seam). Nothing is deferred to a big-bang final integration.

The most exhaustive, defect-by-defect mapping to §6 of any proposal: capability-on-wire drift, Publisher-bit clobber, sequential search, admission inversion, first-token lookup, ZIM ReaderAt shim, trusted-publisher demotion, reputation-feedback inconsistency, unified env gate, partial rate-limit update are each tied to a specific key_decision.

capability.Announced(Sharing,RuntimeFacts) as the SINGLE producer of the 64-bit services mask, consumed by both swarmsearch's peer_announce and httpapi's ServicesReporter, structurally kills three §6 defects at once (downgrade-not-on-wire, /aggregate static constant, and the drift between them) — this is the cleanest single fix in any proposal.

Splitting operator-settable Sharing from daemon-owned RuntimeFacts so the HTTP setter physically cannot reach the Publisher bit makes the §6.1 'save sharing clobbers Publisher' defect unrepresentable by type, not by discipline.

Extracting a leaf `record` package for SignedRecord/SigMessage/ElementID directly targets the §5.1 latent-bug class (byte-identical RecordID derivation duplicated across swarmsearch/dhtindex/companion) without breaking layer isolation, since record is format-neutral, not a cross-layer response type.

Preserves the legacy's three genuinely-sound structural bets that the SPEC treats as architectural law: strict three-layer isolation with per-layer response types reconciled only at the edge, one daemon.New wiring point, and httpapi with zero subsystem imports.
weaknesses: The 'never send an sn_search frame to a non-advertising peer' rule (§5.1, invariant #1's load-bearing case) stays a per-connection runtime fact plus convention, not a type-level guarantee as in the hexagonal and slice proposals — it is guarded by the wirecompat gate but is structurally weaker than a capability token that makes sending to a bare address uncompilable.

The Layer-D swappability story is a single RecordBackend seam inside dhtindex (legacyKeyword vs aggregatePPMI); the proposal itself flags the risk that if the interface is drawn wrong the §7-C migration re-architects anyway. It lacks the explicit dual-write/dual-read composite that the ≥12-month back-compat contract (§5.2, §2.12) really needs.

RuntimeFacts must be recomputed at exactly the moments live state changes (start publishing, enter regtest, companion up/down); the mitigation (recompute on every peer_announce from engine getters) is sound but depends on engine getters staying truthful, a discipline point rather than a structural one.
Centralizing confirm/flag and search reconciliation in daemon/searchmux risks a fat daemon package; the mitigation (daemon holds only wiring+adapters+two shared ops) is credible but must be held to.
best_ideas_to_graft: capability.Announced() as the ONLY producer of the services mask, shared by the wire announcer and every readout endpoint — adopt regardless of which architecture wins.
Split operator-settable Sharing from daemon-owned RuntimeFacts as distinct types so the HTTP/GUI setter cannot zero the Publisher bit.
A leaf `record` package owning SignedRecord/SigMessage/ElementID with golden vectors, imported by all three layers, to kill the duplicated-byte-derivation hazard.

Promote the MiniPeer + golden-wire-vector conformance suite into the CI merge gate (wirecompat) so invariant #1 is an enforced gate, not a convention — with the timing-sensitive multi-client scenarios kept local-only to avoid re-flaking CI.
One shared daemon.Confirm/Flag path plus one shared searchmux, called by both web and GUI, so frontends cannot drift in reconciliation or feedback semantics.
evaluation.overall: The strongest proposal under the stated weighting. It ships working vertical slices from slice one, carries the least ceremony, and converts the §6 defect classes into structurally-unrepresentable states via a handful of small, well-justified owners rather than a wholesale re-architecture. Its two relative weaknesses — the advertised-peer rule staying convention-plus-gate, and a single-seam Layer-D swap — are real but bounded, and both can be hardened by grafting the capability-token idea from Proposal 2 and a composite dual-read adapter without disturbing the rest of the design. Ranked first.

strengths: The contracts/* tier of pure frozen leaves (bencodec, snsign, sntoken, snrecord, powhash, riblt, dhtschema, snagg, ltepcodec), each with checked-in golden byte vectors, is the single best structural answer to the SPEC's repeated §5.1 warning that byte-identical derivations duplicated across files must stay in sync — it gives each cross-implementation contract exactly one home and makes drift a unit-test failure.

kernel/substrate as a policy-free single owner of the anacrolix client + DHT server + LTEP map, exposing only narrow ports, cleanly resolves the shared-engine coupling risk without a god-object: substrate holds zero capability logic and download becomes a peer slice, collapsing the legacy engine's dozen inbound imports into event emissions plus ports.

Build order is the same shape as the module map — each increment ships a capability a user or peer can immediately observe (download, local search, trust, authoring, DHT search, swarm search, companion, aggregate), so the slices are genuinely vertical rather than a horizontal foundation followed by big-bang integration.

Strong invariant-1 confinement: only two slices ever touch the peer wire and only one touches the DHT, substrate is the sole client owner so no slice can open a UDP port or add a DHT verb, and LtepTransport.Send requires a peer handle that exists only after that peer advertised sn_search — making 'never send to a non-advertiser' a type-level property testable against an in-memory MiniPeer.

Correctly fixes the load-bearing §6 defects: default-deny AdmissionPolicy, one live-caps function feeding both wire and /aggregate + /capabilities with PATCH semantics, MostDistinctive token for Layer-D, verified+attributed companion ingest with GeneratedAt dedup, unified SWARTZNET_UNSAFE gate, and a multi-batch sync driver.
weaknesses: The typed event bus as the PRIMARY cross-slice channel introduces a new load-bearing failure mode — fire-and-forget delivery can drop a FileCompleted under backpressure and silently un-index a file — which is essentially the legacy's fragile file-tracker fan-out re-created as core infrastructure that must be correct from slice one, before any consumer exists. The replay-buffer + hourly-rescan mitigation is exactly the legacy §5.5 mechanism, so the risk is inherited rather than eliminated.

Consumer-defined-interfaces-satisfied-only-at-the-composition-root is disciplined but ceremony-heavy for a small team, and the proposal itself flags that it invites shortcut slice→slice imports that reintroduce cycles; the acyclic guarantee rests on reviewer discipline at the wiring site.

The native Fyne GUI is deferred to a single 'frontend hosts finalize' slice at the very end, and the proposal admits 'each slice owns its frontend end-to-end' is only partly enforceable across the CGO/Fyne boundary — so GUI parity is a convention the compiler will not check and is the closest thing to a deferred integration in this plan.

substrate is the one place all wire flows through; if any slice pushes a scope filter or capability decision down into it, it regresses toward the legacy hub-engine — a risk the proposal acknowledges and can only guard with a lint/review rule.
best_ideas_to_graft: The contracts/* frozen-leaf tier with checked-in golden byte vectors as the one home for every byte-identical wire/crypto primitive — this is a superset of Proposal 1's record package and should be adopted whole.

kernel/substrate as a policy-free single anacrolix/DHT owner exposing only narrow ports, so download is a consumer slice rather than the integration hub — even if the winning design is not fully slice-based, this cleanly contains the MPL surface and the anacrolix quirks.
The framing 'only two slices touch the peer wire, only one touches the DHT' as an explicit, reviewable confinement invariant for invariant #1.
The hourly rescan-of-completed-files fallback shipping WITH the local-search slice (not later) to preserve the §5.5 dropped-event recovery guarantee.
evaluation.overall: A strong second. Its contracts/* tier and policy-free substrate are the two best individual ideas across all three proposals and should be grafted into any final design. The vertical build order is genuine and its wire confinement is structurally sound. It loses to Proposal 1 on simplicity because the event bus adds a genuinely new load-bearing failure mode (dropped events regressing the §5.5 indexing guarantee) plus consumer-interface ceremony, and because the Fyne GUI is deferred to a finalize slice rather than kept incremental. Ranked second because those costs are real but its excellent primitives make it the closer runner-up.

per_proposal.proposal_name: SwartzNet Hexagonal Rebuild — "The Wire Lives Only in Adapters"

strengths: The strongest structural story for invariant #1: because core and app hold no wire knowledge, every vanilla-observable byte originates in exactly four adapters, and LtepTransport.SendExtension requires a capability-verified peer token minted only from a recorded advertisement — so 'never send sn_search to a non-advertising peer' is a compile-time guarantee, and the whole wire-compat matrix runs against an in-memory VanillaPeer with no sockets. This is the cleanest realization of the load-bearing constraint of any proposal.

The best Layer-D swappability seam: KeywordDirectory as one port with legacy, aggregate, and composite implementations, where the composite expresses the ≥12-month dual-write/dual-read back-compat contract (§5.2, §2.12) as an adapter with ZERO app/domain change, selectable by one line in node.New. RecordCodec as a separate port keeps record bytes codec-owned. This directly answers §7-C without re-architecting.

Identity handled as a core entity behind an IdentityVault port whose Load result carries an isDefaultPath flag, making 'auto-create only at the XDG default, never regenerate implicitly' (invariant #2) a domain policy with one enforcement site.
httpapi structurally cannot import engine/companion because the driving adapters depend only on driving ports — so the §5.8 layer-isolation law is automatic rather than enforced by review.

Fixes the §6 defects at the app/domain layer where they are trivial to place correctly (concurrent SearchService, default-deny bloomPolicy, companion attribution + verification, first-token→MostDistinctive).
weaknesses: Heaviest ceremony of the three: a ports package with 12 driven + 8 driving interfaces, a separate app orchestration layer, and core/* split into seven packages, all sitting below the kernel. For a project whose defining reality is anacrolix's leaky quirks, this is a large abstraction tax that the stated judging lens ('penalize cleverness that raises rebuild risk', 'is module count justified or ceremony') counts against.

The SwarmEngine port is admitted by the proposal itself to risk 'becoming anacrolix-shaped' and to be unable to abstract away the async-under-client-lock constraint, dual 256-slot semaphores, VerifyData rehash, positive-burst rate limiter, and seed-in-place FilePathMaker (§5.4). A wide port over quirks that cannot be hidden is the worst case for a port: it ossifies around one implementation while still paying the indirection cost.

The build order front-loads risk: S0 is 'pure hexagon + offline CLI' — core/* plus all ~20 port interfaces plus in-memory adapters — a large horizontal skeleton delivered before any download/daemon vertical value. When anacrolix reality lands in S1, the SwarmEngine and LtepTransport ports are the likeliest to need reshaping, meaning the most expensive-to-change artifact (the port contracts) is committed earliest with the least validation. That is a higher integration-risk profile than either other proposal.

The extra app hop between the driving ports and the driven ports adds a layer of indirection for every use case, which is pure overhead for the many capabilities that are essentially pass-throughs to a single adapter.
best_ideas_to_graft: LtepTransport.SendExtension requiring a capability-verified peer token minted only from a recorded sn_search advertisement — turning 'only advertised peers' from a runtime check into a type guarantee. This is the single most valuable idea to graft into Proposal 1, which otherwise leaves that rule as convention.

The composite KeywordDirectory adapter that implements dual-write + legacy-then-aggregate dual-read behind one port, so the §5.2 ≥12-month migration is an adapter selection with no app/domain change — graft this to strengthen Proposal 1's single RecordBackend seam.

The in-memory VanillaPeer test double implementing the transport port to run the four-direction wire-compat matrix in-process with no netem, backed by the real anacrolix-v1.61.0 interop scenario as belt-and-suspenders.
IdentityVault.Load returning an isDefaultPath flag so 'auto-create only at default, load-only for explicit --identity' is a single domain rule.
evaluation.overall: Conceptually the most rigorous on invariant safety and Layer-D swappability — its capability-token transport and composite directory adapter are the best individual ideas for those two concerns and should be grafted into the winner. But under a judging lens that weights rebuild feasibility and simplicity above all, it ranks third: the full ports/app/core hexagon is the heaviest ceremony, the SwarmEngine port fights anacrolix quirks the proposal concedes it cannot abstract, and the S0-first build order commits the most expensive, hardest-to-reshape artifact (all ~20 port contracts) before a single download has validated their shape. The right move is to keep Proposal 1's structure and import this proposal's two best seams, not to adopt the hexagon wholesale.

build_order_issues: PLAN Slice 0 introduces `swartznet serve` and has `swartznet status` start its own daemon. This contradicts SPEC §5.10 ('there is NO daemon/serve subcommand; `swartznet add` IS the daemon, and every thin-client command — status/search/flag/confirm/index/files — assumes a running `add` at --api-addr') AND the architecture's own Assumption I51 ('add-as-daemon stays the design'). If `serve` is throwaway scaffolding it must be explicitly retired/folded into `add` in Slice 2; as written the plan ships a non-spec CLI surface and a status command that violates its thin-client contract. Fix: build the Slice-0 lifecycle spine behind `add` (or a clearly-labeled temporary `serve` that Slice 2 deletes) and make `status` a thin HTTP client from the start.

Slice 9 (Layer D, regtest DHT) is not observable end-to-end because the DHT test config surface is unspecified anywhere in ARCHITECTURE. SPEC §5.11/§5.8 make three settings load-bearing for an isolated regtest DHT: DisableIPv6=true and ListenHost=127.0.0.1 (the BEP-44 write-token is SHA1'd over the query's SOURCE IP; a 0.0.0.0 bind lets the kernel flap source IP per send → silent 'invalid token' → value-not-found), plus a placeholder bootstrap 127.0.0.1:1 (an empty DHTBootstrapAddrs falls through to anacrolix's public routers and poisons the isolated cluster). The config module never enumerates ListenHost/DisableIPv6/DHTBootstrapAddrs. Fix: add them to Config + the in-process DHT harness and record the source-IP-pinning rationale, or Slice 9's DoD ('node A publishes, node B searches via BEP-44') cannot pass.

Slice 6 (capability) claims to fix 'capability downgrades never reach the wire', but at Slice 6 there is no wire (Layer S is Slice 7) and RuntimeFacts fields (Publishing←Slice 9, Reconciliation←Slice 8, CompanionPub/Sub←Slice 10) have no live source yet. The leaf is testable in isolation (golden vector + HTTP readout), but the headline wire-reflection fix genuinely spans Slices 6→7 and the single-producer-consumed-by-both-wire-and-readout invariant is unprovable until Slice 7 wires the outbound peer_announce. Acceptable, but the plan should state the fix completes in Slice 7 rather than in Slice 6.

Minor: Slice 2's defect note says the Bloom gate 'arrives in Slice 6'; Bloom actually arrives in Slice 5 (Slice 6 is capability). Harmless but should be corrected so the promotion-decoupled-from-Bloom rationale points at the right slice.

coverage_gaps.what: The offline `swartznet aggregate build|inspect|find` CLI (SPEC §2.1, §2.3, §2.7, §2.11, §3.1, §5.10) is owned by no module and shipped by no slice. It is a real, tested, fully-offline (no daemon/DHT) capability: sign+optionally-mine-hashcash+pack a JSONL record set into a signed SNAGG B-tree (mode 0644), print records/pages/bytes/fingerprint; `inspect` prints trailer metadata failing on bad magic/version/trailer-sig; `find --verify` runs a prefix query and re-derives the fingerprint; `--pow-bits>40` is refused (exit 2); `--piece-size` MUST match the wrapping torrent's piece length. `contracts/snagg` owns the bytes but nothing owns the sign/mine/pack/inspect/find orchestration or the CLI wiring. Slice 12 builds the SNAGG format and Aggregate backend but its module list omits `cmd/swartznet` aggregate subcommands entirely.
coverage_gaps.fix: Assign the aggregate subcommands to a module (cmd/swartznet + a thin offline builder over contracts/snagg + contracts/sign + identity load-only) and add them to Slice 12's Definition of Done, including the --pow-bits>40 refusal and --piece-size-must-match-metainfo rules.

coverage_gaps.what: The `crawl-probe` CLI subcommand (SPEC §2.1, §2.6, §5.10) — a one-shot BEP-51 sample_infohashes probe from a throwaway 127.0.0.1:0 NoSecurity+Passive DHT server, fresh-random target per run, JSON output {addr,target,samples[],interval,num,nodes[]} — is not slotted into any slice. dhtindex is said to own 'BEP-51 crawl primitives' but the probe binary/subcommand has no home.
coverage_gaps.fix: Add crawl-probe to a slice (naturally alongside dhtindex BEP-51 primitives in Slice 9, or with ops tooling in Slice 13) so the shipped CLI surface matches §2.1's dispatch list.

coverage_gaps.what: Sync-session budget enforcement — the wire-compat MUST from §2.12/§5.1: per-session max_symbols/max_bytes negotiated downward (min of peer's budget and own 2000/1MiB defaults), symbol-budget overrun → sync_end 'limit_exceeded', other violations → 'aborted' + misbehavior charge, byte accounting on the SEMANTIC record size (32+kw+20+8+8+64) not bencoded bytes, and sync_symbols.index MUST equal the receiver's running symbols-in count (any mismatch = hard abort) — is not called out in any slice DoD. Slice 8 mentions the multi-batch responder and RIBLT internals but not the budget/limit_exceeded/index-desync guards, which are cross-implementation contracts.
coverage_gaps.fix: Add explicit assertions for downward budget negotiation, limit_exceeded vs aborted taxonomy, semantic-size byte accounting, and sync_symbols.index desync-abort to Slice 8's Definition of Done.

invariant_risks.what: The transport-token graft (invariant #1's strongest structural guard) risks an engine↔swarmsearch import cycle as described. The doc lists `LtepTransport.SendExtension(peer PeerToken, frame []byte)` and `PeerToken` under ENGINE's Key types, while requiring swarmsearch to send every frame through it. But swarmsearch is the CALLER of SendExtension, so if PeerToken/Transport are engine types, swarmsearch must import engine — and engine already imports swarmsearch (inbound-frame dispatch to Handler, handler wiring, LocalSearcher adapter). That is a compile cycle. The legacy avoids it precisely by defining the `Sender`/`LtepAdvertiser` seam IN swarmsearch and sending by a plain address string; the graft's whole value (a bare address is unsendable — you need a token minted from a recorded advertisement) forces the token type to be visible to swarmsearch's call site. If the team 'resolves' this by keeping the token in engine and NOT threading it through swarmsearch, the type-level guarantee silently degrades to convention (the architecture's own Open Risk #4).
invariant_risks.fix: Define the opaque `PeerToken` type and the `Transport`/`SendExtension` interface IN swarmsearch (or a tiny shared contracts leaf), mirroring the legacy Sender seam. Engine mints tokens in its PeerConnAdded/extended-handshake path (only when the remote advertised sn_search in its m-dict — NOT gated on peer_announce, so a token-holding peer that never announced is still answered per §5.1) and injects an implementation of swarmsearch's Transport. State this ownership explicitly in ARCHITECTURE so the DAG claim is provable and engine→swarmsearch stays one-directional.

invariant_risks.what: Slice 0 DoD 'binding to a non-loopback address is refused' tightens invariant #3 beyond what the spec documents. SPEC §2.9 and §5.9 (line 899) state the server DOES bind non-loopback addresses if asked ('operators may front their own auth') and emits a loud one-time UNAUTHENTICATED warning; the security model is loopback-bind + CSRF, not a hard refusal. Refusing removes the documented ListenHost / `--api-addr 0.0.0.0` capability. This is a defensible invariant-hardening but it is an unrecorded behavior change (no assumption logged for it).
invariant_risks.fix: Either keep the warn-and-bind behavior (loopback default, non-loopback allowed with a loud warning) to match §2.9/§5.9, or record the refusal explicitly as a deliberate tightening of invariant #3 in the Assumptions section so it isn't a silent divergence.

rules_lost: §5.5 MIME resolution consults SwartzNet's extTypes override map BEFORE stdlib mime.TypeByExtension. This is load-bearing, not cosmetic: Go's builtin table lacks .txt, so on Alpine/scratch deployments plaintext extraction silently skips EVERYTHING without the override, and .ts must resolve to TypeScript not MPEG-TS; stdlib results also need any ';charset=' suffix stripped. Not surfaced in the indexer/extractors design — a golden/table test candidate.

§5.6 signature-verification taxonomy is three-way, not two: missing snet fields → ErrNotSigned (benign); crypto failure → ErrBadSignature (firm tamper, struct still populated); but wrong pubkey/sig LENGTHS → a plain error that is NEITHER sentinel. The architecture (contracts/sign, signing) names only ErrNotSigned/ErrBadSignature; UIs distinguish benign-vs-tamper on this taxonomy, so the third case must be preserved.

§5.5 raw .html/.htm files are indexed by the PLAINTEXT extractor with tags left in (text/html is in plaintext's accept list); the tag-stripping HTML walker is used ONLY for XHTML inside EPUB/ZIM. There is deliberately no standalone HTML extractor. A rebuild that 'improves' this by adding a proper HTML extractor silently changes indexed content for every .html file (§7-Q40).

§5.2 keywords whose UTF-8 salt exceeds 64 bytes are DROPPED, never truncated (truncation would alias distinct keywords onto one DHT target). Not called out in contracts/dhtschema or contracts/token; must be preserved as a hard drop.

§5.9 the web UI injects Bleve highlighter fragments and highlighted names via innerHTML on the explicit assumption that Bleve pre-escapes text and only adds <mark> tags. A rebuild of either the highlighter or the web UI that drops that escaping guarantee becomes a stored/reflected XSS. Not mentioned in the httpapi/web design.
defect_regressions: No §6.1 verified defect is re-encoded — the architecture's defect-class table is thorough and each fix is structural. Two watch-items to keep from regressing during implementation: (1) Companion's SignedBy-stamp fix coexists with the preserved §5.5 shared local/remote doc-ID namespace (last-write-wins). A local add of infohash X after a companion import (or vice versa) still overwrites t:X, so the SignedBy attribution can be dropped on the later write; the fix must ensure the followed-publisher stamp survives or that local docs deliberately take precedence (§7-Q37 is open — pick and note a default). (2) The L1 in-swarm fix must keep the fail-closed property §5.1 line 733 guarded: when ShareLocal==1 and a query targets a torrent NOT in the active swarm, the swarm-filtered searcher must return nothing rather than fall back to the full index — otherwise fixing the '§6 L1 shares nothing' defect reintroduces the over-serve leak the fail-closed reject-code path was protecting against.
critique.verdict: APPROVE WITH REQUIRED FIXES. The architecture and plan are strong, spec-faithful, and correctly turn most §6 defect classes into unrepresentable-by-construction fixes while preserving the load-bearing §5 rules and all four invariants. No dependency cycle is confirmed and no §6 defect is re-encoded. Four items must be resolved before/at their slices: (1) HIGH — pin transport-token/PeerToken ownership in swarmsearch (not engine) so the invariant-#1 structural guard doesn't force an engine↔swarmsearch cycle or silently degrade to convention; (2) HIGH — give the offline `aggregate build/inspect/find` CLI a module and a Slice-12 DoD (currently orphaned); (3) MEDIUM — reconcile the plan's `serve`/status-as-daemon skeleton with SPEC §5.10 and Assumption I51 (add-is-daemon); (4) MEDIUM — specify the regtest-DHT config surface (ListenHost/DisableIPv6/placeholder bootstrap) so Slice 9 is observable. Address the low/medium rules-lost items (extTypes-before-stdlib, 3-way sig taxonomy, plaintext-HTML, salt>64 drop, innerHTML/Bleve-escaping) as explicit preservation notes/golden vectors, and record the non-loopback-refusal and /capabilities-publisher-field-drop as logged assumptions."
